Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	"""HTTP server exposing the ledger REST API using the Python standard library."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import json
5	from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
6	from urllib.parse import parse_qs, unquote
7	
8	from .service import LedgerService
9	from .store import valid_idempotency_key
10	
11	MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1 << 20  # 1 MiB cap on request bodies
12	
13	# Token-gated checkpoint-history routes. Every request to one of these is
14	# rejected before the body is read or any state is touched unless the node was
15	# started with --history* and the request authenticates: the configured static
16	# bearer token is full-power, or the active persisted credential presents a
17	# token hash covering the route's permission. POST /v1/history/access manages
18	# that credential and is reserved for the static token.
19	HISTORY_ROUTES = {
20	    ("GET", "/v1/history/trust"),
21	    ("POST", "/v1/history/trust"),
22	    ("POST", "/v1/history/export"),
23	    ("POST", "/v1/history/access"),
24	}
25	
26	
27	def build_handler(service: LedgerService) -> type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
28	    """Create a handler class closed over the given ledger service."""
29	
30	    class LedgerHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
31	        server_version = "VerifiableLedger/1.0"
32	
33	        # -- helpers --------------------------------------------------------
34	
35	        def _send_json(
36	            self, status: int, body: dict, sort_keys: bool = True
37	        ) -> None:
38	            data = json.dumps(
39	                body, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=sort_keys
40	            ).encode("utf-8")
41	            self.send_response(status)
42	            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
43	            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
44	            self.end_headers()
45	            self.wfile.write(data)
46	
47	        def _history_authorized(self, method: str, path: str) -> bool:
48	            """Bearer-token gate for the /v1/history/* routes.
49	
50	            Returns True when the request may proceed. When the feature is
51	            disabled the gate is open (the service answers 404); otherwise the
52	            request is authenticated before the body is read or any state is
53	            touched. The configured static token is full-power; an active
54	            persisted credential whose token hash matches is admitted only for
55	            routes covered by its permission set. A missing/malformed/unknown
56	            bearer is answered 401 (``unauthorized``); an authenticated
57	            credential lacking the route's permission is answered 403
58	            (``forbidden``). Both failures happen without reading the body,
59	            appending an audit event or touching any file.
60	            """
61	            if (method, path) not in HISTORY_ROUTES:
62	                return True
63	            if not getattr(service, "history_enabled", False):
64	                return True
65	            required = service.history_route_permission(method, path)
66	            provided = self.headers.get("Authorization")
67	            outcome = service.authorize_history(provided, required)
68	            if outcome == "ok":
69	                return True
70	            error = "unauthorized" if outcome == "unauthorized" else "forbidden"
71	            self._send_json(
72	                401 if error == "unauthorized" else 403,
73	                {"ok": False, "error": error},
74	                sort_keys=False,
75	            )
76	            # The body was deliberately not consumed: close the connection so
77	            # an unread Content-Length body cannot desync the next pipelined
78	            # request on a keep-alive socket.
79	            self.close_connection = True
80	            return False
81	
82	
83	        def _read_json(self) -> tuple[bool, object]:
84	            try:
85	                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
86	            except ValueError:
87	                return False, {"error": "invalid Content-Length"}
88	            if length <= 0:
89	                return False, {"error": "request body must be JSON"}
90	            if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
91	                return False, {"error": "request body too large"}
92	            raw = self.rfile.read(length)
93	            try:
94	                return True, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
95	            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
96	                return False, {"error": "request body must be valid JSON"}
97	
98	        # -- uniform request idempotency ------------------------------------
99	
100	        def _idempotency_key(self) -> "str | bool | None":
101	            """Resolve the Idempotency-Key header.
102	
103	            Returns None when the header is absent (verbatim legacy behavior),
104	            False when it is malformed (repeated header or a value outside
105	            1..128 visible ASCII characters), otherwise the key string.
106	            """
107	            values = self.headers.get_all("Idempotency-Key")
108	            if not values:
109	                return None
110	            if len(values) != 1 or not valid_idempotency_key(values[0]):
111	                return False
112	            return values[0]
113	
114	        def _drain_mutation_body(
115	            self, has_key: bool
116	        ) -> tuple[bool, object]:
117	            """Drain (and, with a key, parse) a body on a body-less mutation.
118	
119	            Without an Idempotency-Key the behavior is verbatim legacy: any
120	            present body is drained through the same reader as before and its
121	            parse result is ignored. With a key the body is part of the
122	            request fingerprint, so it must be valid JSON (empty -> None);
123	            invalid JSON or an oversized body is a 400 sentinel.
124	            """
125	            if not has_key:
126	                if self.headers.get("Content-Length"):
127	                    self._read_json()
128	                return True, None
129	            try:
130	                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
131	            except ValueError:
132	                return False, {"error": "invalid Content-Length"}
133	            if length <= 0:
134	                return True, None
135	            if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
136	                return False, {"error": "request body too large"}
137	            raw = self.rfile.read(length)
138	            try:
139	                return True, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
140	            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
141	                return False, {"error": "request body must be valid JSON"}
142	
143	        def _send_mutation_result(
144	            self,
145	            status: int,
146	            body: dict,
147	            key: str,
148	            replayed: bool,
149	            cached_text: str | None,
150	            sort_keys: bool,
151	        ) -> None:
152	            """Send an idempotent mutation response.
153	
154	            On the first 2xx and on every replay the cached text is the exact
155	            on-wire JSON (first and replay are byte-identical) and both
156	            Idempotency-Key and Idempotency-Replayed (false/true) are echoed.
157	            Any other answer (business 4xx/5xx, conflict) is sent verbatim
158	            with no idempotency headers, exactly like a keyless request.
159	            """
160	            if cached_text is None:
161	                self._send_json(status, body, sort_keys=sort_keys)
162	                return
163	            data = cached_text.encode("utf-8")
164	            self.send_response(status)
165	            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
166	            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
167	            self.send_header("Idempotency-Key", key)
168	            self.send_header(
169	                "Idempotency-Replayed", "true" if replayed else "false"
170	            )
171	            self.end_headers()
172	            self.wfile.write(data)
173	
174	        def _mutation(
175	            self,
176	            method: str,
177	            key: "str | bool | None",
178	            action,
179	            body: object,
180	            sort_keys: bool = True,
181	        ) -> None:
182	            """Dispatch one state-changing route with uniform idempotency.
183	
184	            No header: the action runs and answers exactly as before. A
185	            malformed header is 400 with no state touched. A valid key runs
186	            the request through the service idempotency gateway, which
187	            serializes same-key concurrency on the store lock, replays the
188	            cached 2xx on a matching fingerprint, answers 409 on a changed
189	            method/target/body, and never occupies the key on a non-2xx answer.
190	            """
191	            if key is False:
192	                # The body may still be unread on a body-less mutation route:
193	                # close the connection so it cannot desync the next pipelined
194	                # request on a keep-alive socket.
195	                self.close_connection = True
196	                self._send_json(400, {"error": "invalid Idempotency-Key"})
197	                return
198	            if key is None:
199	                status, result = action()
200	                self._send_json(status, result, sort_keys=sort_keys)
201	                return
202	            status, result, replayed, cached_text = service.execute_idempotent(

"""HTTP server exposing the ledger REST API using the Python standard library."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, unquote

from .service import LedgerService
from .store import valid_idempotency_key

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1 << 20  # 1 MiB cap on request bodies

# Token-gated checkpoint-history routes. Every request to one of these is
# rejected before the body is read or any state is touched unless the node was
# started with --history* and the request authenticates: the configured static
# bearer token is full-power, or the active persisted credential presents a
# token hash covering the route's permission. POST /v1/history/access manages
# that credential and is reserved for the static token.
HISTORY_ROUTES = {
    ("GET", "/v1/history/trust"),
    ("POST", "/v1/history/trust"),
    ("POST", "/v1/history/export"),
    ("POST", "/v1/history/access"),
}


def build_handler(service: LedgerService) -> type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
    """Create a handler class closed over the given ledger service."""

    class LedgerHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        server_version = "VerifiableLedger/1.0"

        # -- helpers --------------------------------------------------------

        def _send_json(
            self, status: int, body: dict, sort_keys: bool = True
        ) -> None:
            data = json.dumps(
                body, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=sort_keys
            ).encode("utf-8")
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(data)

        def _history_authorized(self, method: str, path: str) -> bool:
            """Bearer-token gate for the /v1/history/* routes.

            Returns True when the request may proceed. When the feature is
            disabled the gate is open (the service answers 404); otherwise the
            request is authenticated before the body is read or any state is
            touched. The configured static token is full-power; an active
            persisted credential whose token hash matches is admitted only for
            routes covered by its permission set. A missing/malformed/unknown
            bearer is answered 401 (``unauthorized``); an authenticated
            credential lacking the route's permission is answered 403
            (``forbidden``). Both failures happen without reading the body,
            appending an audit event or touching any file.
            """
            if (method, path) not in HISTORY_ROUTES:
                return True
            if not getattr(service, "history_enabled", False):
                return True
            required = service.history_route_permission(method, path)
            provided = self.headers.get("Authorization")
            outcome = service.authorize_history(provided, required)
            if outcome == "ok":
                return True
            error = "unauthorized" if outcome == "unauthorized" else "forbidden"
            self._send_json(
                401 if error == "unauthorized" else 403,
                {"ok": False, "error": error},
                sort_keys=False,
            )
            # The body was deliberately not consumed: close the connection so
            # an unread Content-Length body cannot desync the next pipelined
            # request on a keep-alive socket.
            self.close_connection = True
            return False


        def _read_json(self) -> tuple[bool, object]:
            try:
                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
            except ValueError:
                return False, {"error": "invalid Content-Length"}
            if length <= 0:
                return False, {"error": "request body must be JSON"}
            if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
                return False, {"error": "request body too large"}
            raw = self.rfile.read(length)
            try:
                return True, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                return False, {"error": "request body must be valid JSON"}

        # -- uniform request idempotency ------------------------------------

        def _idempotency_key(self) -> "str | bool | None":
            """Resolve the Idempotency-Key header.

            Returns None when the header is absent (verbatim legacy behavior),
            False when it is malformed (repeated header or a value outside
            1..128 visible ASCII characters), otherwise the key string.
            """
            values = self.headers.get_all("Idempotency-Key")
            if not values:
                return None
            if len(values) != 1 or not valid_idempotency_key(values[0]):
                return False
            return values[0]

        def _drain_mutation_body(
            self, has_key: bool
        ) -> tuple[bool, object]:
            """Drain (and, with a key, parse) a body on a body-less mutation.

            Without an Idempotency-Key the behavior is verbatim legacy: any
            present body is drained through the same reader as before and its
            parse result is ignored. With a key the body is part of the
            request fingerprint, so it must be valid JSON (empty -> None);
            invalid JSON or an oversized body is a 400 sentinel.
            """
            if not has_key:
                if self.headers.get("Content-Length"):
                    self._read_json()
                return True, None
            try:
                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
            except ValueError:
                return False, {"error": "invalid Content-Length"}
            if length <= 0:
                return True, None
            if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
                return False, {"error": "request body too large"}
            raw = self.rfile.read(length)
            try:
                return True, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                return False, {"error": "request body must be valid JSON"}

        def _send_mutation_result(
            self,
            status: int,
            body: dict,
            key: str,
            replayed: bool,
            cached_text: str | None,
            sort_keys: bool,
        ) -> None:
            """Send an idempotent mutation response.

            On the first 2xx and on every replay the cached text is the exact
            on-wire JSON (first and replay are byte-identical) and both
            Idempotency-Key and Idempotency-Replayed (false/true) are echoed.
            Any other answer (business 4xx/5xx, conflict) is sent verbatim
            with no idempotency headers, exactly like a keyless request.
            """
            if cached_text is None:
                self._send_json(status, body, sort_keys=sort_keys)
                return
            data = cached_text.encode("utf-8")
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
            self.send_header("Idempotency-Key", key)
            self.send_header(
                "Idempotency-Replayed", "true" if replayed else "false"
            )
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(data)

        def _mutation(
            self,
            method: str,
            key: "str | bool | None",
            action,
            body: object,
            sort_keys: bool = True,
        ) -> None:
            """Dispatch one state-changing route with uniform idempotency.

            No header: the action runs and answers exactly as before. A
            malformed header is 400 with no state touched. A valid key runs
            the request through the service idempotency gateway, which
            serializes same-key concurrency on the store lock, replays the
            cached 2xx on a matching fingerprint, answers 409 on a changed
            method/target/body, and never occupies the key on a non-2xx answer.
            """
            if key is False:
                # The body may still be unread on a body-less mutation route:
                # close the connection so it cannot desync the next pipelined
                # request on a keep-alive socket.
                self.close_connection = True
                self._send_json(400, {"error": "invalid Idempotency-Key"})
                return
            if key is None:
                status, result = action()
                self._send_json(status, result, sort_keys=sort_keys)
                return
            status, result, replayed, cached_text = service.execute_idempotent(
                method, self.path, key, body, action, sort_keys=sort_keys
            )
            self._send_mutation_result(
                status, result, key, replayed, cached_text, sort_keys
            )

        def _json_mutation(
            self, method: str, action, payload: object, sort_keys: bool = True
        ) -> None:
            """Resolve the key for a JSON-body mutation route and dispatch it."""
            key = self._idempotency_key()
            self._mutation(method, key, action, payload, sort_keys=sort_keys)

        # -- routing --------------------------------------------------------

        def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 (stdlib naming)

                ok, payload = self._read_json()

            elif path.startswith("/v1/transactions/") and path.endswith(

        def do_DELETE(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 (stdlib naming)
            path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
            if path.startswith("/v1/trust/allowlist/"):
                # DELETE /v1/trust/allowlist/{source} — a body is not part of
                # the route; without an Idempotency-Key the request behaves
                # verbatim (no body is read, as before). With a key the body
                # is drained and parsed so it can form the fingerprint.

def serve(service: LedgerService, host: str, port: int) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
    """Create and run the HTTP server (blocks until interrupted)."""
    httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), build_handler(service))
    httpd.serve_forever()
    return httpd

14	      "audit_events":      optional append-only hash-chained event list,

16	      # omits them and is accepted as legacy):

34	  when recorded, else the default endowment);

36	  plus the ``audit_checkpoint`` pinning the log head (an absent event list

38	* when the trust extensions are present: ``trust_sources`` as a

181	def verify_snapshot(document: object) -> dict:
182	    """Verify the internal consistency of one decoded snapshot document.
183	
184	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "error": None, "generation", "height", "tip_hash",
185	    "state_root", "audit_checkpoint"}`` on success, or the same shape with
186	    ``ok`` False, ``error`` set to ``"input"``/``"integrity"`` and every other
187	    field null. Never raises for malformed input.
188	    """
189	    try:
190	        if not isinstance(document, dict):
191	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
192	        result = _verify(document)
193	    except _Failure as failure:
194	        return _failed(failure.category)
195	    except Exception:
196	        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs report rather than crash.
197	        return _failed(ERR_INPUT)
198	    return {
199	        "ok": True,
200	        "error": None,
201	        "generation": result["generation"],
202	        "height": result["height"],
203	        "tip_hash": result["tip_hash"],
204	        "state_root": result["state_root"],
205	        "audit_checkpoint": result["audit_checkpoint"],
206	    }

209	def _verify(data: dict) -> dict:
210	    # Unknown top-level keys make the document shape wrong; the five
211	    # extension sections plus the optional audit log are the only extras.
212	    allowed = set(REQUIRED_SECTIONS) | set(KNOWN_OPTIONAL_SECTIONS)
213	    for key in data:
214	        if key not in allowed:
215	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
216	    for section in REQUIRED_SECTIONS:
217	        if section not in data:
218	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
219	
220	    state = data["state"]
221	    chain_raw = data["chain"]
222	    pending_raw = data["pending"]
223	    index_raw = data["index"]
224	    accounts_raw = data["accounts"]
225	    checkpoint_raw = data["audit_checkpoint"]
226	
227	    # -- core section types --------------------------------------------------
228	    if not isinstance(state, dict):
229	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
230	    if not isinstance(chain_raw, list) or not chain_raw:
231	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
232	    if not isinstance(pending_raw, list):
233	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
234	    if not isinstance(index_raw, dict):
235	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
236	    if not isinstance(accounts_raw, dict):
237	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
238	
239	    generation = state.get("generation", 0)
240	    if not _is_int(generation) or generation < 0:
241	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
242	    endowment = state.get("initial_balance")
243	    if endowment is not None and (
244	        not _is_int(endowment) or endowment <= 0
245	    ):
246	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
247	    if endowment is None:
248	        endowment = DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE
249	    recorded_state_root = state.get("state_root")
250	    if recorded_state_root is not None and not isinstance(recorded_state_root, str):
251	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
252	
253	    # -- chain recomputation -------------------------------------------------
254	    blocks, seen_tx_ids = _recompute_chain(chain_raw)
255	    # The per-sender sequenced nonce stream is a structural chain invariant:
256	    # each block's per-sender nonce set continues the stream from the lower
257	    # blocks with no gap, inversion or duplicate.
258	    try:
259	        LedgerStore.replay_sequenced_nonces(blocks)
260	    except ValueError:
261	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
262	
263	    # -- mempool --------------------------------------------------------------
264	    pending_txs = _verify_pending(pending_raw, seen_tx_ids)
265	
266	    tip = blocks[-1]
267	    if state.get("height") is not None and state["height"] != tip.height:
268	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
269	    if state.get("tip_hash") is not None and state["tip_hash"] != tip.block_hash:
270	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
271	    if (
272	        state.get("tip_status") is not None
273	        and state["tip_status"] != tip.status
274	    ):
275	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
276	
277	    # -- derived index / accounts / state root -------------------------------
278	    expected_index, expected_accounts = _compute_derived(blocks)
279	    _verify_index(index_raw, expected_index)
280	    _verify_accounts(accounts_raw, expected_accounts)
281	
282	    # -- optional derived sequenced-transfer reservations --------------------
283	    _verify_sequences(data.get("sequences"), blocks, pending_txs)
284	
285	    leaves = [
286	        crypto.account_state_leaf(account, balance, transactions)
287	        for account, balance, transactions in LedgerStore.account_state_rows(
288	            blocks, endowment
289	        )
290	    ]
291	    state_root = crypto.account_state_root(leaves)
292	    if recorded_state_root is not None:
293	        # A non-string was an input error above; a wrong-length/non-hex string
294	        # or a digest mismatch is corruption of the stored artifact.
295	        if not crypto.is_hex64(recorded_state_root) or recorded_state_root != state_root:
296	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
297	
298	    # -- audit hash chain and checkpoint -------------------------------------
299	    checkpoint, events = _verify_audit(data.get("audit_events"), checkpoint_raw)
300	
301	    # -- trust extensions (registry, allowlist, key history) ------------------
302	    _verify_trust(
303	        data.get("trust_sources"),
304	        data.get("allowlist"),
305	        data.get("source_key_history"),
306	        events,
307	    )
308	
309	    # -- persistent permissioned history credential --------------------------
310	    _verify_history_credential(data.get("history_credential"), events)
311	
312	    # -- uniform Idempotency-Key records --------------------------------------
313	    _verify_idempotency(data.get("idempotency"))
314	
315	    return {
316	        "generation": generation,
317	        "height": tip.height,
318	        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
319	        "state_root": state_root,
320	        "audit_checkpoint": checkpoint,
321	    }

324	def _recompute_chain(chain_raw: list) -> tuple[list[Block], set[str]]:
325	    """Parse and re-verify the canonical chain straight from the raw JSON.
326	
327	    Field presence/type defects are input errors; every recomputed mismatch
328	    (heights, prev_hash links, tx_ids, signatures, ordering, Merkle roots,
329	    block hashes, genesis/pending-status rules) is an integrity error.
330	    """
331	    blocks: list[Block] = []
332	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
333	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(chain_raw):
334	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
335	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
336	        for key in _BLOCK_KEYS:
337	            if key not in block_raw:
338	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
339	        height = block_raw["height"]
340	        prev_hash = block_raw["prev_hash"]
341	        merkle_root = block_raw["merkle_root"]
342	        block_hash = block_raw["block_hash"]
343	        txs_raw = block_raw["transactions"]
344	        status = block_raw.get("status", STATUS_CONFIRMED)
345	        # Raw types are checked before any use: a string/float/bool height or
346	        # amount is never coerced into the integer it resembles.
347	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
348	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
349	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
350	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
351	        if not isinstance(merkle_root, str) or not isinstance(block_hash, str):
352	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
353	        if not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
354	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
355	        if not isinstance(status, str):
356	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
357	        if status not in (STATUS_PENDING, STATUS_CONFIRMED):
358	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
359	
360	        if height != position:
361	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
362	        expected_prev = (
363	            GENESIS_PREV_HASH if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
364	        )
365	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
366	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
367	        if position == 0 and (
368	            status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or txs_raw
369	        ):
370	            # Genesis is born confirmed and carries no transactions.
371	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
372	        if position < len(chain_raw) - 1 and status == STATUS_PENDING:
373	            # Pending blocks may only sit at the chain tip.
374	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
375	
376	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
377	        for tx_raw in txs_raw:
378	            tx = _parse_transaction(tx_raw)
379	            if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
380	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
381	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx.tx_id)
382	            tx_ids.append(tx.tx_id)
383	
384	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
385	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
386	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
387	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
388	        if compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root) != block_hash:
389	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
390	        try:
391	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
392	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
393	            # Every field was validated above; reaching here still means the
394	            # stored block document cannot represent the recomputed block.
395	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
396	    return blocks, seen_tx_ids
397

399	def _parse_transaction(tx_raw: object) -> Transaction:
400	    """Validate one raw transaction document and recompute tx_id/signature.
401	
402	    Missing keys or non-plain-integer/non-string field types (including a
403	    non-positive amount) are input errors; a recomputed tx_id or Ed25519
404	    signature mismatch is an integrity error.
405	    """
406	    if not isinstance(tx_raw, dict):
407	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
408	    for key in _TX_KEYS:
409	        if key not in tx_raw:
410	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
411	    sender = tx_raw["from"]
412	    recipient = tx_raw["to"]
413	    amount = tx_raw["amount"]
414	    signature = tx_raw["signature"]
415	    stored_tx_id = tx_raw["tx_id"]
416	    if not isinstance(sender, str) or not isinstance(recipient, str):
417	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
418	    if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
419	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
420	    if not isinstance(signature, str) or not isinstance(stored_tx_id, str):
421	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
422	    try:
423	        tx = Transaction.from_dict(tx_raw)
424	    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
425	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT) from None
426	    if stored_tx_id != tx.tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
427	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
428	    if not crypto.verify_signature(tx.sender, tx.message, tx.signature):
429	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
430	    return tx

433	def _verify_pending(pending_raw: list, chain_tx_ids: set[str]) -> dict[str, Transaction]:
434	    """Mempool entries are well-formed, unique, and disjoint from the chain.
435	
436	    Returns the parsed mempool keyed by tx_id so the derived sequences view
437	    can be recomputed.
438	    """
439	    pending: dict[str, Transaction] = {}
440	    for tx_raw in pending_raw:
441	        tx = _parse_transaction(tx_raw)
442	        if tx.tx_id in pending:
443	            # Duplicate pending transaction in the mempool.
444	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
445	        if tx.tx_id in chain_tx_ids:
446	            # A mempool transaction already sealed into a block.
447	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
448	        pending[tx.tx_id] = tx
449	    return pending

452	def _compute_derived(
453	    blocks: list[Block],
454	) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[str, dict]]:
455	    """Confirmed-only tx_id -> height index and per-account activity.
456	
457	    Mirrors ``LedgerStore._compute_derived`` exactly (including a self-send
458	    listing its tx_id once per side) so the comparison can never disagree on
459	    an artifact the node itself wrote.
460	    """
461	    tx_index: dict[str, int] = {}
462	    accounts: dict[str, dict] = {}
463	    for block in blocks:
464	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
465	            continue
466	        for tx in block.transactions:
467	            tx_index[tx.tx_id] = block.height
468	            for account in (tx.sender, tx.recipient):
469	                entry = accounts.setdefault(
470	                    account, {"sent": 0, "received": 0, "transactions": []}
471	                )
472	                entry["transactions"].append(tx.tx_id)
473	            accounts[tx.sender]["sent"] += tx.amount
474	            accounts[tx.recipient]["received"] += tx.amount
475	    return tx_index, accounts

480	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not _is_int(value) or value < 0:
481	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
482	    if raw != expected:
483	        # Any extra, missing or remapped confirmed-transaction entry is a
484	        # derived-data inconsistency.
485	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

488	def _verify_accounts(raw: dict, expected: dict[str, dict]) -> None:
489	    for account, entry in raw.items():
490	        if not isinstance(account, str) or not isinstance(entry, dict):
491	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
492	        sent = entry.get("sent")
493	        received = entry.get("received")
494	        transactions = entry.get("transactions")
495	        if not _is_int(sent) or not _is_int(received) or not isinstance(transactions, list):
496	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
497	        if any(not isinstance(tx_id, str) for tx_id in transactions):
498	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
499	    if raw != expected:
500	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

503	def _verify_sequences(
504	    raw: object, blocks: list[Block], pending_txs: dict[str, Transaction]
505	) -> None:
506	    """Verify the optional derived ``sequences`` section.
507	
508	    The section is a pure derived view of the sequenced transfers in the chain
509	    (confirmed plus the pending tip) and the mempool; its shape is an input
510	    concern and any disagreement with the recomputed view, a non-dense nonce
511	    partition, or a section missing while sequenced transfers exist is
512	    integrity corruption.
513	    """
514	
515	    def parse_pairs(value: object) -> dict[int, str]:
516	        if not isinstance(value, list):
517	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
518	        pairs: dict[int, str] = {}
519	        previous = -1
520	        for item in value:
521	            if not isinstance(item, dict) or tuple(item.keys()) != ("nonce", "tx_id"):
522	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
523	            nonce = item["nonce"]
524	            tx_id = item["tx_id"]
525	            if not _is_int(nonce) or nonce < 0:
526	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
527	            if not isinstance(tx_id, str) or not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id):
528	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
529	            if nonce <= previous:
530	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
531	            pairs[nonce] = tx_id
532	            previous = nonce
533	        return pairs
534	
535	    try:
536	        expected = LedgerStore.compute_sequence_state(blocks, pending_txs)
537	        LedgerStore.validate_sequence_partitions(expected)
538	    except ValueError:
539	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
540	
541	    if raw is None:
542	        if expected:
543	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
544	        return
545	    if not isinstance(raw, list):
546	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
547	    parsed: dict[str, dict] = {}
548	    for entry in raw:
549	        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or tuple(entry.keys()) != (
550	            "account",
551	            "confirmed",
552	            "pending",
553	        ):
554	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
555	        account = entry["account"]
556	        if not isinstance(account, str) or not account:
557	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
558	        if account in parsed:
559	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
560	        parsed[account] = {
561	            "confirmed": parse_pairs(entry["confirmed"]),
562	            "pending": parse_pairs(entry["pending"]),
563	        }
564	    if parsed != expected:
565	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

568	def _verify_audit(events_raw: object, checkpoint_raw: object) -> tuple[dict, list[dict]]:
569	    """Validate the optional event hash chain and the mandatory checkpoint.
570	
571	    A present ``audit_events`` section must be a list of objects whose dense
572	    1..N ids, prev_hash links and event_hash digests all recompute; the
573	    checkpoint (required even with no event list) must pin the recomputed log
574	    head, or the all-zero root for an empty log. Chain/checkpoint defects are
575	    integrity errors; the section/value types are input errors. Returns the
576	    checkpoint summary and the validated event list (empty when the section
577	    is absent) for the trust cross-checks.
578	    """
579	    if events_raw is None:
580	        events: list[dict] = []
581	    else:
582	        if not isinstance(events_raw, list):
583	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
584	        if any(not isinstance(event, dict) for event in events_raw):
585	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
586	        events = events_raw
587	        try:
588	            audit.validate_event_chain(events)
589	        except audit.AuditChainError:
590	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
591	
592	    if not isinstance(checkpoint_raw, dict):
593	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
594	    if set(checkpoint_raw) != {"event_id", "event_hash"}:
595	        # The checkpoint is exactly {event_id, event_hash}; any extra or
596	        # missing key makes its shape wrong.
597	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
598	    event_id = checkpoint_raw["event_id"]
599	    event_hash_value = checkpoint_raw["event_hash"]
600	    if not _is_int(event_id) or event_id < 0:
601	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
602	    if not isinstance(event_hash_value, str):
603	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
604	    try:
605	        audit.validate_checkpoint(checkpoint_raw, events)
606	    except audit.AuditChainError:
607	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
608	    return {"event_id": event_id, "event_hash": event_hash_value}, events

611	def _verify_trust(
612	    trust_raw: object,
613	    allowlist_raw: object,
614	    history_raw: object,
615	    events: list[dict],
616	) -> None:
617	    """Validate the trust extension sections against each other and the log.
618	
619	    Every section is optional (a pre-feature snapshot omits them); a present
620	    section is strictly validated. Field presence and raw JSON primitive types
621	    are input errors; value-format, ordering and uniqueness defects, and any
622	    disagreement between the key history, the trust registry and the audit
623	    log's source-key lifecycle events, are integrity errors.
624	
625	    The registry is always reconciled against the event log: every registry
626	    source must have a complete, well-formed lifecycle (register -> rotates ->
627	    at most one revoke), its latest version/public key and its revoked status
628	    must agree with the log, and every lifecycle event must name a registry
629	    source — orphan sources/events and missing events are integrity failures.
630	    A snapshot predating ``source_key_history`` omits that one section: the
631	    registry/event checks still run, but there is no persisted history array to
632	    cross-check (the history is reconstructed in memory by the node instead).
633	    """
634	    registry = _parse_trust_sources(trust_raw)
635	    _parse_allowlist(allowlist_raw)
636	    expected = _reconstruct_key_history(registry, events)
637	    if history_raw is None:
638	        # Legacy snapshot without the section: the registry/allowlist and the
639	        # registry/event reconciliation above still apply, but there is no
640	        # persisted history array to cross-check.
641	        return
642	    history = _parse_source_key_history(history_raw)
643	    for source, entries in history.items():
644	        if source not in registry:
645	            # A history item whose source is absent from the registry is
646	            # orphan data; the persisted sections must agree bidirectionally.
647	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
648	        if entries != expected[source]:
649	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
650	    for source in registry:
651	        if source not in history:
652	            # Current snapshots write one history item per registered source.
653	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
654

656	def _parse_history_credential(raw: object) -> dict:
657	    """Validate a persisted history credential's raw JSON shape.
658	
659	    Exactly ``{version, token_hash, permissions, status}``: a non-boolean
660	    non-negative integer version, a 64-char lowercase hex token hash, a
661	    non-empty duplicate-free list drawn from read/update/export and an
662	    active/revoked status. Missing/extra keys or wrong primitive types are
663	    input errors; invalid digest/permission/status values or an out-of-order
664	    permission list are integrity errors. Returns a normalized response-ordered
665	    dict.
666	    """
667	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
668	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
669	    if set(raw.keys()) != set(HISTORY_CREDENTIAL_KEYS):
670	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
671	    version = raw["version"]
672	    token_hash = raw["token_hash"]
673	    permissions = raw["permissions"]
674	    status = raw["status"]

676	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

791	    permissions while flipping status to revoked. A malformed event payload is

793	    present section with no events, or vice versa, is too).

797	    for event in events:
798	        if event.get("kind") != EVENT_HISTORY_CREDENTIAL_CHANGED:
799	            continue
800	        saw_event = True
801	        action = event.get("action")
802	        try:
803	            change = _parse_history_credential(
804	                {
805	                    "version": event.get("version"),
806	                    "token_hash": event.get("token_hash"),
807	                    "permissions": event.get("permissions"),
808	                    "status": event.get("status"),

820	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

826	                replayed is None

828	                or change["version"] != replayed["version"]
829	                or change["token_hash"] != replayed["token_hash"]
830	                or change["permissions"] != replayed["permissions"]
831	            ):
